svg.text: Pauses and holds: how run_log_sections() builds the sections
Synthetic run logs (the unit-test fixtures) put through pycorn.run_log_sections; start: 5 ml/min, 0 %B.
Numbered marks: run-log entries, listed under each case with their stored (elapsed) time; the x axis is the wall clock CADET uses.
pause: zero-flow section, length = the pause
1. Pause during a ramp, with an instruction logged at the pause
Stored time stops; the pause is inserted as its own section. %B stays at 25 and the ramp goes on after it. The flow change logged at 120 s acts after the pause.
wall-clock s from method start (pauses included)
The flow keeps running and can change; the %B ramp stops where it is. A Gradient issued during the Hold waits and acts at the Continue.
wall-clock s from method start (pauses included)
The first Continue ends the pause only; the run is back in the Hold. The %B step waits for the second Continue.
wall-clock s from method start (pauses included)
A Hold issued during a Pause takes over from it; the next Continue ends the Hold.
wall-clock s from method start (pauses included)
